workflows.title: WF1 Suspicious sign-in
workflows.description: Decide whether a user's account is compromised. MFA fatigue, password spray, impossible travel.
intro:
**Use when:** Lead A on the triage queue, or a user reports MFA prompts they did not start.  
**You need:** the user name (top of the page).  
**Goal:** decide whether this account is compromised. About 5 minutes.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

evidence.title: Push log, oldest first
evidence.expr: {service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | user="$user" | event_type="user.mfa.push" | line_format "{{.outcome}} {{.reason}}  from {{.src_ip}} {{.src_country}} {{.src_city}}  app={{.app}}" | keep service_name

card.look: denied pushes over time, then the push log in order.
card.bad: 3 or more denied or timed-out pushes within about 10 minutes, followed by a SUCCESS.
card.if_bad: note the source IP of the success and go to Step 2.
card.if_clean: one or two failures then a success from the usual device is a fumble. Still do Step 3.

steps.title: Where did the sign-in come from?

evidence.title: Sign-in and VPN sources for this user
evidence.expr: topk(25, sum by (service_name, src_ip, src_country, outcome, user_agent) (count_over_time({service_name=~"secdemo-idp|secdemo-vpn"} | json | user="$user" [$__range])))

card.look: every source the user signed in from, with country and client.
card.bad: a country the user does not work in, a hosting or residential IP nobody else uses, or a script client (`python-requests`, `curl`).
card.if_bad: this is the attacker's address. Copy it into the case timeline and go to Step 3.
card.if_clean: US or MX home and office addresses with a normal browser are expected.

evidence.title: High-risk attempts against this user
evidence.expr: sum by (src_ip, src_country, outcome, reason, user_agent) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | user="$user" | risk_level="HIGH" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Users hit by script-client sign-ins
evidence.help: Breadth of the spray. Every one of these users needs a password check, not just this one.

card.look: high-risk sign-in attempts against this user, and how many other users the same spray hit.
card.bad: a SUCCESS or `PASSWORD_OK_MFA_REQUIRED` from a spray address. The password is compromised even if MFA held.
card.if_bad: the password must be reset regardless of anything else. Continue to Step 4.
card.if_clean: no high-risk attempts against this user. The sign-in may still be bad if Step 1 or 2 was red.

steps.title: Can the user be in two places?

evidence.title: Badge and VPN, oldest first
evidence.expr: {service_name=~"secdemo-badge|secdemo-vpn"} | json | user="$user" | line_format "{{.service_name}}  {{or .door .event}}  {{.site}}  {{.src_country}} {{.src_ip}}  hip={{.hip_compliant}}" | keep service_name

card.look: badge reads and VPN connections for this user, in time order.
card.bad: a badge read at a US site within an hour of a VPN connect from abroad, or `hip_compliant=false` (device failed the posture check).
card.if_bad: the remote session is not the user. Treat as compromised. Go to Step 5.
card.if_clean: badge and VPN tell one consistent story.

evidence.title: Hosts this user was active on (click to open WF2)
evidence.expr: topk(10, sum by (host) (count_over_time({service_name=~"secdemo-edr|secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | host!="" [$__range])))

evidence.title: Uploaded to file sharing
evidence.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range]))

card.look: the hosts this user was active on, privilege changes made to the account, and uploads.
card.bad: a host with EDR detections, the user added to a group, or large uploads.
card.if_bad: click the host to open WF2. If uploads are large, open WF4 from the Decide step.
card.if_clean: ordinary activity on the user's own workstation.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Compromised** if Step 1 or Step 3 was red **and** Step 2 or Step 4 was red.

**If compromised, do these now:**
1. Revoke all IdP sessions and refresh tokens for the user.
2. Reset the password and force MFA re-enrolment.
3. Block the source IP from Step 2 at the IdP and VPN.
4. Open a case and add the user, IP and hosts to it.

**Then go to:**
- WF2 for each host in Step 5 (click it in the table)
- [[WF4 Data exfiltration]] if Step 5 showed uploads
- [[Case timeline]]

**Not compromised:** close the lead with a note on which step cleared it.

rule.close_if_false: Not compromised. Close the lead with the step that cleared it.
